The carrier wave frequently causes the Z-function to stay very small over
a wide span of zeros. In that region a slight perturbation would cause many
zeros to fall off the critical line. Maybe attempts to computationally disprove
RH should begin by looking for regions where the initial terms in the Riemann-
Siegel formula mostly cancel to nothing?

after.text:
14.5 Gram points are of transient interest
A recent paper of Shanker [105] used computational data for the ζ-function to
make two conjectures about Gram intervals, and to suggest that “Gram points
have interesting properties which distinguish them from random points on the
critical line”. We examine that work in the context of the Principles, reaching
a different conclusion.
